newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Renault workers block Eurostar to London.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Renault workers block Eurostar to London.

text.p: Several hundred workers from French carmaker Renault's doomed Belgian plant blocked the Brussels to London Eurostar train at the Belgian capital's South Station on Monday in protest at the plant's closure.

The workers from the Vilvoorde plant near Brussels, estimated by a Reuter photographer at the scene to number between 200 and 300, placed baggage trolleys across the line in front of the train, threw firecrackers and chanted.
Others sat on the platform playing cards and taking light refreshments.
The workers also blocked the high-speed Thalys train connecting Brussels and Paris.
Police were present in large numbers outside the station, but were keeping a low profile inside.
Vilvoorde workers have occupied the car plant since the shock announcement by Renault Chairman Louis Schweitzer on February 27 that the profitable factory would be closed by July.
In concert with workers from France and Spain, the Vilvoorde employees have taken their fight to numerous Renault plants in France.

A week ago between 50,000 and 100,000 trades unionists and politicians from across Europe -- led by the Vilvoorde workers -- marched through Brussels in protest at rising job losses, inhumane firms and uncaring governments.
More such events are planned over the next three months, culminating in a march on Amsterdam on June 14 -- the eve of the European Union's summit to conclude the rewriting of the Maastricht treaty.
The unions have demanded that promotion of job creation be included in the new version.
